summary: Extends re-presentation to prose and research output (claim extraction, citation verification pipelines, numeric registries, summary-first reading). Then lays out staged recommendations: this week cap units near 200 LOC and sessions at 60-90 minutes, require self-explanation blocks, name a human of record; this quarter adopt spec-driven review, adversarial second-model pass, package validation, risk tiering; ongoing, auto-generate summaries and track churn. Gives thresholds that trigger tighter review and closes with caveats on vendor sources, 2006-era data, and preprint status.

claims.text: Hallucinated legal citations have produced sanctions in more than a thousand tracked cases worldwide.
If AI PR defect or churn exceeds ~1.5x human baseline, tighten to full line-by-line review and shrink chunks.
Approval faster than ~300-500 LOC/hour signals rubber-stamping and should trigger friction.
The 200-400 LOC and 60-90 minute limits come from 2006 human-code data, not re-derived for AI diffs.
EASE 2026's 64.53% figure merges evaluative and workflow comments, so it is not pure substantive review.

risks.note: 'More than a thousand tracked cases' has no tracker or source named.
The 1.5x and 300-500 LOC/hour thresholds are author-chosen, no derivation given.
Numeric registry approach recommended with no evidence it works in practice.

least_confident: Whether the Stage 2 and 3 thresholds are backed by any study or are the author's judgment calls.
